B. Is this measure already running in Lapland wellbeing services county (or in the OYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Precise radiotherapy (SBRT) for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated. Every stage I patient who is too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy (3-8 visits, no anaesthesia) instead of being left without treatment. The treatment exists in every university hospital; what is missing in some counties is the referral rule.
effect_summary_en: In the Netherlands, 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated once stereotactic radiotherapy became available. That is a share of one subgroup, so it supports roughly 0.6 points of all patients only through our own 8% assumption.
supported_en: A Netherlands registry study (Haasbeek et al., Annals of Oncology 2012) found 7% fewer untreated elderly stage I patients once the treatment was available.
not_supported_en: No page shows the effect on the share of all lung cancer patients, or any Finnish or Lapland-specific gap.
in_use_quote: Paikallisessa tai paikallisesti edenneessä taudissa, jos leikkaushoito ei ole mahdollista, voidaan antaa täsmäsädehoitoa tai yhtä aikaa säde- ja solunsalpaajahoitoa eli kemosädehoitoa.
in_use_summary_en: OYS's lung cancer care pathway says stereotactic radiotherapy can be given when surgery is not possible, and that the university hospital runs the multidisciplinary lung cancer meetings and gives the surgery and radiotherapy for the area.
missing_en: No page shows a rule that every frail stage I patient from Lapland is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy.
summary_en: OYS's lung cancer care pathway says stereotactic radiotherapy can be given to patients who cannot be operated, and that OYS runs the multidisciplinary meetings and gives the radiotherapy. No page shows a rule that refers every eligible patient. A Netherlands registry study (Annals of Oncology 2012) found 7% fewer untreated elderly stage I patients once the treatment was available. That supports the direction of the effect, but the share of all patients rests on our own assumption.
unanswered_en: I found no Lapha (Lapland county) or OYS page with a referral rule, and no figure on how many inoperable stage I patients in Lapland go untreated.
